_why: Which benchmarks a change makes worth re-running. Deliberately coarse: a benchmark run for nothing costs minutes, one not run hides a regression, so the globs are directories and over-include on purpose. 'benchmarks' are BenchmarkDotNet classes, measured against themselves; 'harnesses' are the cross-language pairs, which is where the claim against rapidfuzz is actually measured. tools/check_bench_map.py refuses either kind if this file does not name it. A harness also names the corpus generators it needs: those corpora are written rather than committed, and a runner has none of them. CrossLang/ is not one 'always' unit (#351): Harness.cs is the base every cross-language file builds on, but each comparison's own file -- PersistenceCrossLang.cs, MetricsCrossLang.cs, and so on -- belongs to that one harness's own sources, not to all four. Measured: a single line added to PersistenceCrossLang.cs previously matched 'always' and selected all of them -- 15 benchmark classes at the time -- and all 4 harnesses; it now selects one. 'diagnostics' are the third kind: subcommands that answer a question a lot asks once, so the nightly deliberately never runs them and they carry no sources. They are listed anyway, because a bench_*.py that nothing names is otherwise indistinguishable from a harness somebody forgot to map -- which is the finding this file exists to raise.
_why_dispatch_only: Program.cs is in 'always' for the BenchmarkSwitcher call every class goes through, not for the switch above it: a dispatch arm names a subcommand the nightly never runs, so adding one used to select all 16 classes for zero information (#465). select_benchmarks.py compares the two revisions with the named construct removed, and lets the file trigger 'always' only when something outside it moved. The construct is named here rather than hard-coded there, so a file that stops having a switch stops being exempt instead of silently staying so, and so does one that grows a second. The anchor is the statement -- the keyword starting a line, followed by '(' -- not the bare word, which also occurs in the comment above the switch and used to make whatever block followed that comment the exempt region (#480). tools/check_bench_map.py refuses this key when the file it names is gone or no longer holds exactly one of the construct.
